issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal contradiction about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: it requires that the stock be static (shared across instances) but also instructs students to initialize attributes (including stock) "in the constructor of SealSaloon". A static (or static final) field cannot be correctly initialized in an instance constructor, so following the instructions literally would lead to compilation errors or confusion. The reference solution initializes the static final stock at declaration (not in the constructor), which resolves the conflict but the problem text remains inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement to make the intended initialization approach consistent: either (A) require stock to be static (shared) and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock();), or (B) require stock to be an instance final field and keep the instruction to initialize it in the constructor. Update the text that mentions constructor initialization or the note about stock being static so both are consistent.
